question.:question/problem:
Write the equation of this circle in the form $(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The equation of a circle with radius $r$  centered at the point $(a,b)$ in rectangular coordinates in standard form is

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

In our case, the circle is centered at $(3,0)$ and the radius of the circle is $r=3$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-3)^{2}+(y-0)^{2} & ={3}^{2} \\ (x-3)^{2}+{y}^{2} & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the circle in rectangular coordinates is 

$$
(x-3)^{2}+{y}^{2}=9.
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ is 

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

Let's compare the general equation to our equation side-by-side as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-5)^{2}+{y}^{2} & =3 \\ (x-5)^{2}+(y-0)^{2} & ={(\sqrt{3})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We see that $a=5,$ $b=0,$ and $r=\sqrt{3}.$ 

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(5,0)$ and its radius is $\sqrt{3}.$
